input:
A binomial random variable X satisfies 9.p(X = 4) = p(X = 2) when n = 6. Then p is equal to

Options:
A. 1/4
B. 1/2
C. 1/8
D. 1/5

phase_1_understand_the_problem.problem_restatement: For a binomial random variable X ~ B(n=6, p), find parameter p given that 9 P(X = 4) = P(X = 2).
phase_1_understand_the_problem.key_observation: Use the binomial PMF P(X = k) = ⁿCₖ pᵏ qⁿ⁻ᵏ with n = 6. Note ⁶C₄ = ⁶C₂ = 15, which cancel out from both sides.

key_concepts: Binomial PMF formula: P(X = k) = ⁿCₖ pᵏ (1-p)ⁿ⁻ᵏ
Relation between p and q: q = 1 - p

key_formulas.pmf_4: P(X = 4) = ⁶C₄ p⁴ q² = 15 p⁴ q²
key_formulas.pmf_2: P(X = 2) = ⁶C₂ p² q⁴ = 15 p² q⁴
key_formulas.equation: 9 (15 p⁴ q²) = 15 p² q⁴  ⇒  9 p² = q²

phase_3_plan_the_approach.strategy: Write expressions for P(X=4) and P(X=2), substitute into 9 P(X=4) = P(X=2), cancel common factors 15 p² q², take square root, replace q with 1-p, and solve for p.
logical_steps: Step 1: Write P(X=4) = 15 p⁴ q² and P(X=2) = 15 p² q⁴
Step 2: Equate 9 (15 p⁴ q²) = 15 p² q⁴
Step 3: Divide by 15 p² q² (since 0 < p, q < 1) to get 9 p² = q²
Step 4: Take positive square root: 3p = q
Step 5: Substitute q = 1 - p: 3p = 1 - p ⇒ 4p = 1 ⇒ p = 1/4
